editorial:
If you love sports stories that feel personal instead of flashy, this documentary pulls you in fast. It follows Stephen Curry as he nears his 4,000th career three-pointer, but the real draw is how it connects that huge milestone to his childhood, family, and daily habits. You see the pressure, the joy, and the quiet work behind the highlight reels, with interviews and behind-the-scenes moments that make the whole journey feel warm and human.

The pacing stays lively without rushing, and the mix of game footage, family memories, and honest reflection keeps you engaged. A few sections repeat familiar sports-doc beats, and some viewers may want more locker-room drama, but the heart and focus make up for it. If you enjoy uplifting true stories about discipline and belief, this is an easy recommendation. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the sharpest picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Curry reaches the 4,000th three-pointer during a tense game, then the film shifts to a quiet family moment where he explains that the number matters less than the people who shaped him. The twist is that the documentary was never only about a record; it is about how his parents, faith, and daily practice turned doubt into confidence. You leave seeing the milestone as a symbol of years of steady work.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves uplifting sports stories and behind-the-scenes athlete profiles.
